claims.text: The precursor is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy composition.
Ink-extrusion additive manufacturing can use the stated mixture of metallic powders and TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 precursors to form HfNbTaTiZr.
In-situ alloy formation from mixed powders is feasible during additive manufacturing of refractory multi-principal-element alloys.
The hydrides decompose in the sequence TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, then ZrH2.
Differences in hydride formation enthalpy drive the proposed decomposition sequence.
A reactive Ti getter preferentially scavenges oxygen evolved during hydride decomposition.
The getter reaction forms stable TiO or TiO2 that sequesters oxygen.
In NbMoTaWVTi, oxygen introduced during processing produces an FCC precipitate identified as TiO.
Dissolved oxygen stabilizes alpha-HCP or alpha-Ti phases in HfNbTaTiZr.
Ti scavenging lowers matrix oxygen activity below a critical threshold for alpha-HCP nucleation.
A sintering range of 1200–1400 °C balances the decomposition kinetics of the five hydrides.
A vacuum below 10^-3 Pa is appropriate for preventing oxygen contamination during sintering.
Cooling faster than 100 °C/s bypasses the alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC transformation window.
Rapid quenching from the homogenization temperature preserves a metastable single-phase beta-BCC HfNbTaTiZr structure.
The proposed processing route produces a relative density above 99%.
The rapidly quenched alloy has a grain size below 1 µm.
Suppressing grain-boundary pinning by oxide inclusions refines the grain size to the sub-micron scale.
Slow cooling produces a dual alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC phase constitution.
Ung gettered or insufficiently scavenged material can contain TiO precipitates.
The Ti getter must have sufficient stoichiometric capacity to capture all oxygen through the final hydride-decomposition step.

contradictions.description: TiO/TiO2 formation and corresponding diffraction peaks are proposed as confirmation that the getter works, yet significant TiO in the final material is defined as evidence of getter failure. The hypothesis does not specify a location or quantity criterion that distinguishes desirable oxide confined to the getter layer from undesirable matrix precipitates.

Sub-micron refinement is attributed to suppression of oxide-related grain-boundary pinning, while the proposed mediator deliberately creates stable Ti oxides. Moreover, suppressing pinning would ordinarily permit rather than inhibit grain growth; no alternative refinement mechanism is supplied.
